findings.claim: The lab plan says no lab needs PostgreSQL and the F23 JDBC project is tested only against H2. That cannot validate the frozen F23 objective "Connecting Java to Postgres with JDBC": pgJDBC uses its own driver and jdbc:postgresql URL, while embedded H2 uses an H2 driver/database URL. The planned project therefore verifies generic JDBC mechanics but not the named PostgreSQL integration.

evidence.section: Initializing the Driver; Connecting to the Database (pgJDBC service loading, jdbc:postgresql URLs, DriverManager.getConnection)
Database URLs; Embedded and In-Memory modes (jdbc:h2 URLs)

findings.recommendation: Keep the no-container rule, but make the F23 course lab use the learner-local PostgreSQL installation through pinned pgJDBC. Have the single Maven test command create an isolated schema or database, run the tests, and clean it up using documented environment-based connection settings on macOS, Linux and Windows. H2 may remain for fast unit tests, but it must not be the only solved-run proof for the PostgreSQL connection/repository objective.

findings.claim: The queries lab says it covers all eight module topics by running learner SQL and the seed script against H2, but seeding objective o3 requires psql \copy. PostgreSQL documents \copy as a psql frontend meta-command, not SQL sent through JDBC, so an H2/JDBC execution harness cannot execute or validate that objective.

evidence.section: Meta-Commands: \copy; documented as a frontend (client) copy performed by psql
PostgreSQL Compatibility Mode; in-process H2 compatibility settings and supported differences

findings.recommendation: Either run the seed-script path through real psql against learner-local PostgreSQL from the one Maven entry command, or narrow the H2-executed lab scope to portable SQL and provide a separately validated real-psql exercise for o3. Do not claim the H2 runner covers all eight topics unless the manifest identifies and tests the non-SQL psql path.

findings.claim: The normalization objectives assert anomaly and decomposition behavior, but the frozen topic sources cover PostgreSQL keys and referential integrity rather than normalization theory. The intake honestly marks this unverified, so the objectives are not yet source-bound despite the intake saying the official-evidence gap is closed.

evidence.section: 5.5 Constraints (unique, primary-key and foreign-key mechanics; not normalization anomalies or normal forms)
Description of normalization; first, second and third normal forms; redundancy and maintenance problems

findings.recommendation: Add an authoritative first-party normalization source to source-snapshot.json and map its specific sections to o1/o2 before authoring, or keep the source-gap record open. The Microsoft Learn source sampled here is one viable first-party explanation; preserve the PostgreSQL sources for the key/constraint mechanics.
